item.title: Projects
item.description:
My work spans biological oceanography, marine imaging, scientific computing, and the development and application of oceanographic observing technologies.

Current Projects

Icy Seas Co-Laboratory

At the Icy Seas Co-Laboratory, I work at the intersection of marine science, in situ imaging, and scientific computing. My work focuses on developing and supporting tools for the collection, processing, and analysis of oceanographic imaging data.

Current work includes the curation of plankton image datasets, development of image-analysis workflows, and the use of machine learning to improve the detection and segmentation of organisms and particles in marine imagery.

item.title: Research
item.description:
My research interests lie at the intersection of biological oceanography, marine imaging, and scientific computing.

Marine Imaging

I work with in situ imaging systems to observe plankton, particles, and other organisms in the marine environment.

Scientific Computing

I use image processing, machine learning, and computational workflows to analyze large oceanographic imaging datasets.

Field Oceanography

My field experience includes supporting oceanographic research at sea, including scientific instrumentation, sampling operations, and the deployment and recovery of oceanographic equipment.

item.title: About
item.description:
I am a biological oceanographer interested in marine imaging, instrumentation, and computational approaches to studying plankton and marine ecosystems.

My work combines in situ imaging with scientific computing and data analysis to better understand marine organisms and their environment.

Much of my research has taken place at sea, working with oceanographic instrumentation and imaging systems in the Gulf of Alaska, California Current, and North Sea.

item.title: Sea Time
item.description: My field experience includes research cruises across the Gulf of Alaska, California Current, and the North Sea.
